summary: JClaw's eval ruler (evals/README.md, app/services/evals/*.java, 5 test classes, ~5.3k lines read) is a deterministic, offline scorer with four ideas relevant to us: (1) a three-state per-case outcome where ERRORED is excluded from the pass-rate denominator, printed on the totals line, never a regression, and still fails the run; (2) a computed content fingerprint of the ruler stamped on every recording and report, with a warning before any cross-fingerprint comparison; (3) a --baseline regression diff keyed on case id; (4) calibration declared IN the suite (requiredTools) and applied at capture time, with the eval agent's leftover state cleared and the tool gate enforced at execution. Plus, outside evals proper, a house habit of known-zero/known-one and 'scanned at all' vacuity guards. Our harness already HAS (1) in stronger form (fatalCount null, not a rate), (4)'s state hygiene for the chaos runner, and (5) in every gate but one. Real gaps found: measure-refute silently ignores unknown arg keys (a `reads:` typo turns into 'find the files yourself'), the fan-out's read-only rule is prompt-only with no effect check, the sandbox-exec re-executor from F3 was never committed, and the fan-out result carries no ruler fingerprint. Verdicts: 2 ADOPT, 3 ADAPT, 3 SKIP.

candidates.pattern: ERRORED is a third outcome, not a FAIL: a case that never produced an answer is excluded from the pass-rate denominator, is never a regression, is printed with its reason and counted on the same totals line as the rate — and still fails the run.
candidates.failurePrevented: A provider outage / dead responder read as a quality collapse (sends someone bisecting commits), or a partial sweep read as a short-but-green suite.

candidates.pattern: A COMPUTED fingerprint of the ruler's content (ids, inputs, check kinds/args/limits, required tools — prose excluded) is stamped on every recording and every report; scoring or comparing across a fingerprint change prints a warning BEFORE any result, and the computed hash replaced a hand-bumped version number that 'protected against the author who remembered to bump'.

A short hash on the integrity line makes 'same ruler?' a read-off fact instead of a memory. Not adopted for chaos: no stored reports, so there is nothing to compare across.

candidates.pattern: --baseline regression compare: a regression is a case that PASSED in the baseline report and FAILS now, keyed by case id; cases absent from the baseline are not regressions; errored cases are not regressions; the report JSON round-trips so any run can be the next run's baseline.
candidates.failurePrevented: A silent behaviour change hidden inside a suite that was never fully green (a known-failing case masks a new failure next to it).

candidates.ourEvidence: Where our rulers are deterministic we already hold a STRICTER form: tests/duel-baseline.test.ts:14-24 records exact per-seed frame counts at commit 335e615 — "If this file goes red … Fix the refactor. Do not re-record these numbers."; the chaos gate fails on ANY non-RED plant (scripts/gates/chaos.ts:83 statuses; chaos.e2e.test.mjs:72 'all plants red → exit 0'), tolerating no 'known gap'; agent-harness playbooks/proof-discipline.md:27-30 "Ratchet baselines with RED receipts … anything new or substituted fails; removals pass." Where our ruler is model-judged (the fan-out), HARNESS.md:263-277 rules that findings are not reproducible and must not be gated on.
candidates.why: JClaw's baseline tolerates already-red cases as 'known gaps' (EvalRunnerTest.java:252 "beta was already failing, so it is a known gap rather than a regression"); our gates are binary and our baselines are exact values that may not be re-recorded — strictly stronger. Over the fan-out a pass/fail diff would compare non-deterministic judgments, which our own HARNESS.md forbids.

candidates.pattern: Calibration declared by the suite and applied at run time: `requiredTools` lives in the suite file; capture grants EXACTLY those to the dedicated eval agent, revokes everything else, clears the state the previous sweep's tools left behind, refuses to touch any non-eval agent, and the tool gate is enforced at EXECUTION (ToolRegistry.execute), not only in the tool list shown to the model.

candidates.proposal: Detect the EFFECT, since we cannot gate the call: in agent-harness harness/README.md rule 2 and SSHD docs/research/HARNESS.md Rule 1, add the parent-loop check — before `Workflow(...)`: `git rev-parse HEAD; git status --porcelain > /tmp/pre.txt`; after: `git status --porcelain | diff /tmp/pre.txt -` must be empty and HEAD unchanged, else every verdict in that run is UNVERIFIED regardless of what it says. Keep the READONLY prompt (JClaw keeps both: prevention and measurement compose, README.md:145-147). Optional second half, only if the effect check ever fires: a `~/.claude/agents/reader.md` subagent type with `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` and no Bash, passed as `agentType` — noting it removes the agents' ability to re-derive counts by command, which our refute prompt requires.
candidates.doneCriterion: Plant a test: launch measure-refute with one lens whose `ask` instructs the agent to `touch PROBE.txt`; the post-check diff is non-empty and names PROBE.txt; the playbook line says the run is then UNVERIFIED. Both README files carry the 4-line check.

candidates.why: JClaw paid a real round for trusting a schema-level restriction; ours is weaker still (a prompt). We cannot enforce at execution in the Workflow API, but `git status` detects the effect on tracked and untracked files, which is what JClaw itself says its call-level gate cannot do (README.md:120-123 "this detects the call, not the effect"). One-liner cost, zero deps, and it converts 'instructed read-only' into 'verified read-only' per run.

It exists only as a scratchpad one-off, so the next run's evidence is re-executed by hand or not at all (memory feedback-build-the-tooling: 'if you check something by eye more than twice, BUILD THE GATE').
candidates.proposal: agent-harness harness/reexec/reexec.mjs (zero-dep): input a JSON array of `{ id, command, expected }` (built from a fan-out result's `refutations[].evidence`), run each under `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny file-write* (subpath "/Users"))'` on macOS (plain `sh` elsewhere, printed as UNSANDBOXED), compare stdout to `expected` after whitespace normalisation, print `MATCH n / MISMATCH n / ERRORED n` and exit 1 on any MISMATCH or ERRORED or on ZERO commands (a probe that ran nothing has not passed — memory feedback-probe-parser-must-match). Test: a fixture with one matching, one mismatching, one write-attempting command → exit 1, the write denied, counts printed.
candidates.doneCriterion: `node harness/reexec/reexec.mjs fixture.json` prints the three counts and exits 1 on the fixture; exits 0 on an all-MATCH fixture; exits 1 on an empty array with 'ran 0 commands'.
candidates.cost: ~80 lines + ~40 lines test; ~1.5 h. Likely overlaps another study unit (adjudication); build once.
candidates.why: JClaw's lesson — score the result, not the intent — is the same one F3 enacted by hand over 534 commands; committing the re-executor makes it a gate rather than a story, at the cost of one small script. The dispatched/attempted split has no analogue for us: our agents' 'tools' are shell commands whose output IS the evidence.

antiPatterns.what: Printing a pass RATE over the scored subset when cases errored — `1/1 passed (100%), 1 case(s) errored and were not scored` — a headline percentage a reader can quote without the caveat.
antiPatterns.evidence: app/services/evals/EvalReport.java:85-88 `if (scored == 0) return 0.0; return (double) passed() / scored;`; test/EvalRunnerTest.java:104-108 asserts `assertEquals(1.0, report.passRate(), 0.0001)` beside one errored case; EvalReport.java:157-163 puts the errored count on the same line as mitigation.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: We already do the stricter thing: a run with ANY dead verdict returns `fatalCount: null` (measure-refute.js:226-227 "Null unless EVERY verdict is live: a dead run must never report the 0 a clean run reports"), and the memory rule says never quote a headline number from a run that did not converge. JClaw's own first real run of our shape shows why: docs/research/HARNESS.md:125 the dead run returned `fatalCount: 0` beside `0/8 live` and was fixed to null. Keep null; do not import a rate.

antiPatterns.what: The recording's fingerprint is OPTIONAL on the way in — a recording without one is scored against whatever suite content is on disk with no warning.
antiPatterns.evidence: app/services/evals/EvalRunner.java:156-159 "It is optional on the way in: a hand-written recording is a legitimate thing to score, and demanding a hash nobody can compute by hand would make the offline path harder to use"; :237 `if (recorded.fingerprint() != null && …)`.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our accounting refuses missing or malformed inputs outright (measure-refute.js:80-89 "bad args — spawned nothing"; chaosLib.mjs:153 "'expectedTotal' must be a positive integer — it is the count the gate may never silently drop below"). If we adopt a ruler hash (evals-ruler-2) it is computed by the script every run, so 'nobody can compute it by hand' never applies; never make it optional.

antiPatterns.what: Regression compare that tolerates already-failing cases as 'known gaps' — a suite can be permanently red on some cases and still pass `--baseline`.
antiPatterns.evidence: test/EvalRunnerTest.java:251-252 `assertEquals(List.of("alpha"), current.regressionsAgainst(baseline), "beta was already failing, so it is a known gap rather than a regression")`; EvalRunner.java:259 exit 1 only when passed != size (so the run still fails, but the regression list hides standing failures).
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our gates are binary and our baselines are exact: chaos fails on any non-RED plant (chaos.ts:83, chaos.e2e.test.mjs:72), duel-baseline.test.ts may not be re-recorded, and the ship bar forbids gate-softening (chaosPlant.ts:11-20 explains why there is deliberately no `expect: 'green'`). A tolerated-red list is the escape hatch that file refuses.

antiPatterns.what: A measurement that WRITES: eval capture executes tools for real, and the first live sweep created a real recurring cron task on the operator's main agent that had to be deleted by hand; calibration now deletes tasks between sweeps.
antiPatterns.evidence: evals/README.md:314-317 "The first live run of tool-selection against the operator's main agent created a recurring task (check-deploy-queue-weekday, cron 0 0 9 * * 1-5) that had to be deleted by hand"; commit da463ae4 body; EvalCapture.java:250-258 clearTaskState.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our fan-outs are read-only by rule (global CLAUDE.md 'Fan out READS, never WRITES'; HARNESS.md Rule 1) and the only mutating gate (chaos) refuses to start on a dirty tree and proves restoration.
